title: Independent reading: James 2:14–26
subtitle: Follow questions, examples, and repeated claim-and-response structure.
overview: James 2 advances through rhetorical questions, hypothetical examples, objections, and repeated claims about faith and works. Keep each speaker-like move and example boundary clear.
Read the conditional examples as argument illustrations before turning the passage into an abstract system.

items.grc: τί τὸ ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν, ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ;
items.en: What is the benefit, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works?

items.grc: ἡ πίστις, ἐὰν μὴ ἔχῃ ἔργα, νεκρά ἐστιν καθ᾽ ἑαυτήν.
items.en: Faith, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.
